answer: New identities first must pass a memory-bus latency probe: verifier streams a 4 GB working set and demands nanosecond-budget p99 access under 900 ns, a terrace of tight timing no rented cloud VM can fake. Sockpuppets hang like bare vines on a trellis without root, since each fake node needs its own 64 GB RAM floor, roughly $3,200 per identity to provision, and latency jitter exposes shared hosts. First probe passes on warm cache, second cold pass fails. Failure slashes bond and drops identity into an isolated oasis where it earns nothing until re-tested after 72 hours.
